item.title: FastAPI State Management: Accessing Objects via app.state vs request.state
item.description:
“FastAPI State Management: Accessing Objects via app.state vs request.state”

How does one effectively initialize custom objects, such as a NotificationClient, during application startup in FastAPI and subsequently access these objects across different endpoints, potentially defined within separate APIRouter modules? What are the distinctions and trade-offs between utilizing app.state and request.state in conjunction with the modern Starlette lifespan handler?

Sharing State Using app.state with Lifespan Initialization

A straightforward approach involves initializing the required object within a startup routine and attaching it directly to the main application instance via app.state. For cleanup tasks, the shutdown phase of the lifespan handler is employed.

item.title: Solved-how-to-fix-react-usestate-not-updating-immediately
item.description:
“Solved-how-to-fix-react-usestate-not-updating-immediately”

The core of this behavior lies in React’s asynchronous nature of state updates and how JavaScript closures operate within the component’s render cycle. When useState’s setter function is invoked, it doesn’t immediately change the state value for the current render. Instead, it queues an update, and the new state will only be available in the next render cycle of your component.

Let’s dive into various strategies and explanations to effectively manage and fix this “not updating immediately” challenge with React’s useState hook.
